alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ realized by the verse-initial For.
Ordinary conditional ἐάν → if; rule 72's generalizing arm is not in question, no relative or indefinite standing before it.
Supplied expletive subject there is a rule 7/9 helper on the verb; rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical come rather than on the supplied subject.

Preposition realized by into under rule 36. Variant SBLGNT.JAS.2.2.v001 is underdetermined with the projected base among the permitted readings and carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so no textual decision is made here (rules 12, 97).
Genitive pronoun carries the possessive your. The Greek phrase is anarthrous, so rule 20's displacement question does not arise: no article stands here to be emptied.
Anarthrous noun standing bare; the English determiner slot is occupied by your on ὑμῶν.
Anarthrous Greek, so the supplied a is an ordinary rule 51/7 helper on the noun it determines rather than the realization of any article.

One compound adjective rendered by a whole English phrase; with and a ride along as rule 7 helpers, no Greek preposition being expressed. Rule 66's gloss-versus-completion test decides the head: ring glosses the -δακτύλιος stem and gold the χρυσο- element, so neither word is an empty completion and the noun stem the compound is built on takes the head. Rule 91's corpus query cannot settle it, the lexeme being a hapax. A head on gold is defensible if the colour element is read as the salient one; ring is taken because it glosses the compound's head element.
Attributive adjective, reordered before its noun in English under rule 15. The phrase is anarthrous and the ASV supplies no determiner, so rule 58 does not arise.
Noun stands alone; the preposition has its own English word already.
δέ rendered by the connective and; an expressed conjunction, so rules 88 and 98 on a supplied juncture are not in question.

Second occurrence of the same verb, rendered come in. No Greek preposition governs this clause, so the particle in is the compound verb's own and not rule 36's case, unlike s004 εἰς → into in the first clause. Supplied there is a rule 9 helper; head on the lexical come.
Adjunctive καί realized by also. Rule 65 decides an intensifying καί on the English alone — aligned where the ASV writes a word for it — and the ASV writes one here.

Substantival adjective expanded with the generic noun man; rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on the adjective. The Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied a is a rule 7 helper inside the unit.
Attributive adjective rendered vile; here it precedes its noun in the Greek as well, and no determiner is supplied.
Noun stands alone, analysed exactly as the parallel ἐσθῆτι earlier in the verse (rule 24).

review_notes: Reviewed and kept unchanged in substance: every unit's source and target membership, status and head stands as accepted. Notes were expanded where the reasoning was compressed; no ids moved between units.

Partition verified by hand: s001-s018 each appear exactly once, and t001-t027 each appear exactly once across the 18 units. No unrepresented or added unit is needed, since every source token has English and every English word answers to a source token.

s008 χρυσοδακτύλιος is the one head judgment worth flagging, and the note now says why the competing reading was refused: ring glosses the compound's noun stem, gold its modifying element, and rule 91's corpus query is unavailable because the lexeme is a hapax. A head on gold remains defensible.

s012's in is the compound verb's own particle, not a preposition: nothing follows it for an English preposition to govern (the next words are also a poor man), so rule 36 does not reach it. This is deliberately unlike s004, where an expressed εἰς takes into.
Both ἐν phrases are anarthrous with no supplied determiner, so rule 58 is not triggered anywhere in the verse and the adjectives stand on their own English words while the nouns stand bare.

συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν is anarthrous, so your is the genitive pronoun's own under rule 7 and rule 20's displacement analysis has no article to empty. The alternative_rendering note (Or, assembly) is a lexical gloss question and does not bear on the alignment.

Variant SBLGNT.JAS.2.2.v001 is underdetermined, covers s004, keeps the projected base among the compatible readings, and carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 97 does not apply and rule 12 forbids revisiting it here.
